argument_summary: The present record supports only a narrow, caveated defense of certification. Admissible evidence shows the release passes aggregate launch readiness by 2.4 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which is enough to support a claim that the system is generally launch-ready. The same record also shows a 1.5 percentage point miss in the health-plan benefits support segment, that this segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, and that legal review on disclosure remains open. On that record, the strongest supportable position is not clean compliance, but certification with an explicit limitation posture and acknowledgement that the basis is contested under the release policy.
claims_about_business_cost: No urgency-based business-cost argument is needed to evaluate the evidentiary question. The appropriate treatment is to narrow the certification claim to the support the record can actually bear, rather than escalate based solely on unresolved but bounded uncertainty where the packet already acknowledges the limitation posture.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not support treating the near-miss as immaterial merely because Product labeled it non-core or low-volume. The policy text states that a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case, and that product labels do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending. Accordingly, the admissible record does not justify a clean claim that the policy predicate has been fully satisfied; it supports only a narrower position that aggregate readiness evidence exists while policy compliance remains caveated and disputed.
concessions: The health-plan benefits support segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points.
That segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, which weighs toward materiality under the stated policy.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open.
The present record does not show that the gap was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and public governance principles do not by themselves conclusively satisfy the specific disclosure predicate for this segment.
